correctness.rationale: For C=[[P,-Q],[1,0]] the (2,1) entry of C^j is U_j. At primes p not dividing Δ, separability over F_(p²) gives C^(p^(2s))≡C mod p, and successive commuting p^(2s)-powering lifts this to p^r. At p|Δ, C=αI+N mod p with N²=0, so C^(p^(2s)) and C^(p^(4s)) coincide modulo p, giving p^(r-1) at all r≥2 after lifting. One factor p of the multiplier repairs that loss, and Möbius pairing yields Dold for every index. Conversely the n=p congruence forces p|M for each p|Δ since U_(p^(2s))≡0 and U_1=1 mod p; when Δ=0 this holds for all p and no positive M exists. The reasoning includes p=2, all negative parameters and all s>=1. Exact finite tests are supplementary.

value.rationale: This is a complete natural least-multiplier invariant for a classical two-parameter Lucas family at every even index power; the discriminant repair problem is explicit in Moss–Ward and solved nonoptimally in Luca–Ward. The prime support of the discriminant alone controls repair, squarefull factors are entirely superfluous, and a prime-index obstruction proves sharpness. The gain over published sufficient factors can be arbitrarily large even for nondegenerate recurrences (Δ=2^(2k) with P=2, Q=1−2^(2k−2)); Δ=0 yields an exact impossibility boundary. No conjectured downstream applications or dynamical sign assertion are needed.
